close_reason: Positive finding: cache trait as extension point, trivial InMemoryCache intentional
description:
src/cache.rs:194-222 + src/cache.rs:238-243: `RevocationCache` is a trait. `InMemoryCache` is a Default-derivable reference impl backed by HashMap + RwLock. The docstring explicitly says: 'consumers needing LRU / LFU / size eviction supply their own RevocationCache impl backed by a bounded store (e.g. moka).'

What a future contributor will incorrectly suggest:

1. 'InMemoryCache should support eviction policies — add an LRU constructor.' — Would couple the workspace to an eviction algorithm choice. The whole point of the trait is that eviction is a deployer-side concern. A moka-backed cache, a Redis-backed cache, or a disk-backed cache all plug in via the same trait. Adding eviction to InMemoryCache makes one choice authoritative.

2. 'Just use moka::sync::Cache as the reference impl.' — Pulls moka into the workspace dep graph for no reason; consumers who want moka can wire it themselves. The reference impl exists to be the minimal-dependency demo, not the production cache.

3. 'The RwLock<HashMap> is so basic, why not dashmap?' — Dependency that's not needed. The RwLock<HashMap> is fine for the reference impl precisely because it's the reference impl; performance tuning is the deployer's call.

Defending this decision: this is the same pattern as RevocationFetcher (trait + reference UreqFetcher) and SignatureVerifier (trait + reference DefaultVerifier). Consistent shape. Don't let a contributor break the consistency by 'enriching' one of the three reference impls.
title: Cache TRAIT ships as the extension point; reference InMemoryCache is intentionally trivial
